newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta weakens to 84.70/dm amid intervention talk.
newsitem.headline: Peseta weakens to 84.70/dm amid intervention talk.

text.p: The peseta weakened to 84.70 per mark mid-afternoon on Wednesday, hit by French woes, and talk surfaced that the Bank of Spain was intervening to support the currency, dealers said.
The peseta had been trading at around 84.33/38 to the mark early this morning.
The Bank of Spain was not immediately available to comment.

"The weakening extended to the zone of 84.70 per mark, but at this level it stopped which could well have meant the Bank of Spain was intervening, but also could have been the market itself that prevented it from weakening further," a dealer said.
"There are rumours of intervention by the Banks of Portugal and France so it would be strange if the Bank of Spain weren't intervening too."
Other dealers were more convinced that the central bank was intervening at 84.70 per mark.
"They intervened at about 84.65/70," one dealer said.
